answers.explanation: smtp, cs, marshall, edu: four labels. The root is the empty label at the end.
The second-level domain is the part someone registered under the TLD: marshall.edu.
Root servers hold the delegations for every TLD.
Going left adds a level down the tree. `com` delegates `example.com`.
Read right to left: one is under the `au` country TLD, the other under `com`. Different trees, often different owners.
Everything below a delegation belongs to the zone's owner. That's the point of delegating.
Read right to left: the registered domain is `login-check.net`. `marshall.edu` is just a subdomain its owner made up. Attackers count on people reading left to right.
